name: Alport Syndrome Hearing Loss

criteria.description: Positive family history of hematuria, renal failure, or sensorineural hearing loss
Bilateral sensorineural hearing loss, typically progressive and affecting high frequencies
Persistent microscopic hematuria and progressive renal impairment
Presence of anterior lenticonus or other characteristic ocular findings
Identification of pathogenic variants in COL4A3, COL4A4, or COL4A5 genes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of sensorineural hearing loss plus renal involvement and either family history or genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is often clinical but supported by genetic testing and renal biopsy findings.

searchTerms: hearing loss from nerve damage both ears
blood in urine visible only under microscope
tiny amounts of blood in urine

common.symptomName: Sensorineural hearing loss onset in childhood or adolescence
searchTerms: nerve-related hearing loss starting in youth
high blood pressure due to kidney disease

occasional.symptomName: Fatigue related to chronic kidney disease
searchTerms: fatigue linked to chronic kidney failure
low energy due to kidney problems

laboratory: Elevated serum creatinine in progressive renal failure
imaging: Renal ultrasound showing normal or small echogenic kidneys in advanced disease
Ocular slit-lamp examination revealing anterior lenticonus
genetic: Pathogenic variants in COL4A3, COL4A4, or COL4A5 genes
other: Renal biopsy showing irregular thickening and splitting of the glomerular basement membrane

distinguishingFeatures: Isolated microscopic hematuria without progressive renal failure
Absence of hearing loss and ocular abnormalities
No sensorineural hearing loss or ocular findings
Multisystem involvement with obesity, polydactyly, and retinal dystrophy
Hearing loss less common and renal disease differs in pathology

redFlags: Rapidly progressive renal failure in young patient
Early onset bilateral sensorineural hearing loss
Presence of anterior lenticonus on ocular examination
references: Kashtan CE. Alport syndrome: Achieving clarity on the genetic and clinical spectrum. Kidney Int. 2021;99(2):324-326.
